papers.title: Increased aperiodic offset and heightened alpha power characterize resting-state EEG activity in Parkinson's disease
papers.summary: This preprint reports that patients with Parkinson's disease off medication show increased aperiodic offset and alpha power in resting-state EEG compared to healthy controls, which replicated across different EEG systems. Aperiodic parameters also scaled with age and disease duration.

papers.title: Early High-Frequency Network Reorganization After Spinal Cord Stimulation Is Linked to Long-Term Recovery in Disorders of Consciousness.
papers.summary: This study examined source-space EEG network reorganization after spinal cord stimulation (SCS) in 31 chronic disorders of consciousness patients, finding that sustained alpha/beta-band network energy enhancement and beta-band communication consolidation at 1 week and 1 month post-stimulation correlated with 6-month recovery. High-frequency network features, particularly frontoparietal alpha at 1 month, showed the strongest associations with long-term improvement.

papers.title: Associations between EEG measures and clinical severity in CDKL5 deficiency disorder.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This study assessed associations between EEG/evoked potential measures and clinical severity in 77 individuals with CDKL5 deficiency disorder. Resting EEG background slowing (1/f slope and power ratios) correlated with greater symptom severity, but evoked potential measures did not.

papers.title: Normative Modeling of EEG Complexity Reveals Cortical Rigidity Associated with Pain Severity in Chronic Pain.
papers.summary: This study used normative modeling of EEG complexity (Higuchi fractal dimension) in chronic pain patients versus controls. More negative frontal complexity deviations were associated with higher pain intensity, even after adjusting for confounders, suggesting a potential marker for pain severity.

papers.title: Predicting Anxiety Trajectories from Individual Differences in Sleep-Related Distress Alleviation
papers.summary: This cohort study of 223 adults with insomnia and comorbid psychiatric symptoms found that individual differences in the strength of REM sleep-related overnight distress alleviation predicted anxiety improvement over two months, irrespective of treatment or waitlist control. The findings suggest REM-related emotion regulation as a mechanism linking sleep physiology to anxiety recovery.

papers.title: Low-frequency anodal transcranial pulsed current stimulation (0.5-5 Hz): effects on EEG band amplitude, interhemispheric coherence, and cognitive performance.
papers.summary: This crossover study tested low-frequency anodal transcranial pulsed current stimulation (0.5-5 Hz) in healthy adults. 1 Hz stimulation increased interhemispheric coherence in several bands, while other frequencies reduced delta/alpha power, but no changes in cognitive performance were observed.

papers.title: Neurophysiological mechanisms underlying interoceptive hypersensitivity in somatic symptom disorder: a mediation analysis of alexithymia.
papers.summary: This study compared 52 medication-naive somatic symptom disorder patients with healthy controls, finding increased heartbeat-evoked potential amplitudes and resting-state phase lag index in patients, with alexithymia mediating the relationship between HEP amplitude and somatic symptom severity. A combined HEP and alexithymia model achieved good diagnostic discrimination (AUC=0.866).

papers.title: Daily Bowel Movements are Associated with Stronger Gut-Brain Phase-Amplitude Coupling and Better Cognitive Performance
papers.summary: This study investigated the association between bowel movement frequency and gut-brain coupling in women by recording EEG and EGG. They found that women with daily bowel movements had stronger gut-brain phase-amplitude coupling and made fewer cognitive errors, with a path analysis suggesting faecal short-chain fatty acids mediate this coupling.

papers.title: Cognitive exertion reshapes resting-state EEG markers across the adult lifespan
papers.summary: This study examines how cognitive exertion affects resting-state EEG markers across the adult lifespan, finding that post-task recordings show widespread slowing of individual alpha peak frequency and age-dependent changes in the aperiodic exponent. These results demonstrate that these markers are state-dependent and post-task recordings may be useful for indexing individual differences.

papers.title: Entangled criticality and irreversibility in random Markov dynamics.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a random Markov ensemble with parameters for heterogeneity and asymmetry, revealing a critical locus where relaxation times diverge. Applying maximum-likelihood inference to human fMRI and EEG data, they found both modalities operate near this critical point, suggesting superuniversality of brain dynamics.

papers.title: Wearable Morphology-Adaptive in-Ear Device With Active Cleansing Capability for Multimodal Health Monitoring.
papers.summary: This paper reports a wearable in-ear device that self-adapts to ear canal geometry and performs active wax cleaning, enabling stable multimodal recording. It integrates EEG, ECG, and temperature sensors with wireless transmission, reducing sensor-skin impedance by 20%.

papers.title: Peripheral magnetic stimulation effects on brain activity in older adults with schizophrenia - a randomized controlled pilot study.
papers.summary: This randomized sham-controlled pilot study in 40 older adults with schizophrenia found that a single peripheral magnetic stimulation session induced transient resting-state EEG changes, including decreased delta/theta power and increased alpha/beta/gamma power with altered functional connectivity. These exploratory findings suggest potential brain rhythm modulation but require replication in larger trials.

papers.title: Impact of stress on EEG functional connectivity during procedural learning.
papers.summary: This study examined the neurophysiological effects of stress on medical trainees during a procedural learning task using EEG functional connectivity. They found that stress increased functional connectivity compared to calm conditions, suggesting a potential neurophysiological signature of stress that could inform personalized educational interventions.

papers.title: Brain-wide reconfiguration of burst firing by psilocybin reveals 5-HT2A-dependent circuit dynamics
papers.summary: Using simultaneous multi-region Neuropixels recordings in 35 mice, this preprint found that psilocybin selectively reconfigures burst firing, not mean firing rates, across cortex, thalamus, and hippocampus. These burst effects were largely abolished by ketanserin, indicating 5-HT2A receptor dependence.

papers.title: Prediction of subsequent seizures after acute symptomatic seizures in critically ill children: A clinical-electroencephalographic model.
papers.summary: This prospective observational cohort study of 365 critically ill children with acute symptomatic seizures found that subsequent seizure or epilepsy diagnosis occurred in 64%, strongly associated with clinical or electrographic seizures during admission. A simple Seizure/Epilepsy Risk Score showed good discrimination (AUC=0.81), but discharge antiseizure medication use was not associated with different subsequent risk after propensity adjustment.

papers.title: Inkjet-Printed Aqueous Graphene Suspensions on Flexible Substrates for Multimodal Wearable Continuous Health Monitoring.
papers.summary: This paper presents inkjet-printed graphene electrodes on flexible PET substrates for multimodal wearable health monitoring. The electrodes demonstrated high conductivity, durability, and signal quality comparable to commercial gel electrodes, and were used to detect sleep and drowsiness in car drivers.

papers.title: Personality Trait Modulated Panic Emotional Arousal and Physiological Responses in Underground Spaces: A Virtual Reality and Multimodal Measurement Study.
papers.summary: This study developed a personality-modulated panic dynamics framework using virtual reality evacuation experiments with multimodal physiological measurements. They found that personality traits influence physiological responses during panic, and constructed a Panic Composite Index to quantify individual panic intensity.

papers.title: α5-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors regulate state transitions in cortical networks and modulate susceptibility to epileptiform discharges.
papers.summary: The study investigated the role of α5-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in regulating cortical network activity and susceptibility to epileptiform discharges in mice. Knockout of the α5 subunit led to slowed spontaneous cortical activity and reduced susceptibility to spike-and-wave discharges, suggesting a critical role in ictogenesis.

papers.title: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex to subgenual cingulate anticorrelation predicts subgenual cingulate response from prefrontal stimulation.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: This study in depression patients found that stronger resting-state functional connectivity anticorrelation between the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) and subgenual cingulate (SGC) was associated with smaller SGC N100 evoked potential amplitude, suggesting that anticorrelation facilitates modulation of SGC by DLPFC TMS.

papers.title: Morroniside promotes awakening from propofol general anesthesia in gastric cancer surgery by regulating hypothalamic GABAergic neurons.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of gastric cancer, morroniside accelerated recovery of righting reflex after propofol anesthesia without affecting induction, and increased hypothalamic GABAergic neuron calcium signals. Morroniside also modulated EEG power and c-Fos expression, suggesting it promotes awakening via hypothalamic GABAergic neurons.

papers.title: EEG coherence signatures of sport-specific motor imagery in elite freestyle skiing aerials athletes.
papers.summary: This study characterized EEG coherence during sport-specific motor imagery in elite freestyle skiing aerials athletes. They found that high-difficulty imagery elicited stronger theta-band coherence over right-hemisphere connections, and correct judgments were associated with higher high-alpha coherence.

papers.title: Sex differences in propofol-induced loss of consciousness: a clinical study on effect-site concentration and electroencephalographic features.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of surgical patients, females required lower effect-site propofol concentrations to achieve loss of consciousness than males, and exhibited enhanced alpha and delta EEG oscillations. Sex-specific coherence patterns also differed, suggesting sex-specific EEG biomarkers for propofol dosing.

papers.title: Perioperative transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation and EEG biomarkers of sleep improvement after gynecologic laparoscopy: protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This paper describes a randomized controlled trial protocol to evaluate whether perioperative transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation reduces postoperative sleep disturbance in gynecologic laparoscopy patients. The trial will integrate continuous EEG monitoring to explore mechanistic EEG biomarkers.

papers.title: Paroxysmal tonic upgaze mimicking epileptic seizures in infancy: a diagnostic challenge.
papers.summary: This case report describes an 11-month-old infant with paroxysmal tonic upgaze episodes that mimicked epileptic seizures. Normal neurological examination and video EEG without epileptiform activity led to the diagnosis of PTU, highlighting the importance of recognizing this non-epileptic paroxysmal disorder.

papers.title: Evolving epileptic activity under focal rhythmic Delta activity: insights from simultaneous intracranial and scalp EEG.
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared simultaneous intracranial and scalp EEG in six patients with intracranial hematoma to assess whether focal rhythmic delta activity (RDA) on scalp EEG reflects intracranial epileptic activity. They found that while focal RDA on scalp EEG appeared in all cases, intracranial RDA appeared earlier, and spikes, electrographic seizures, and high-frequency oscillations were often not detected on scalp EEG, suggesting that focal RDA may indicate growing epileptic activity and a target for antiseizure therapy.

papers.title: Cognitive risk during underwater exposure: from environmental stressors to assessment and context-aware monitoring.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on cognitive risk during underwater exposure, identifying key stressors such as pressure, breathing gases, thermal stress, and fatigue, and evaluates assessment methods including behavioral tasks, CFFF, EEG/ERP, and HRV. It proposes a staged pathway for future context-aware monitoring and emphasizes the need for prospective validation against operational endpoints.

papers.title: Activity-induced weakening of hippocampal input to prefrontal VIP interneurons reshapes inhibitory microcircuit function: implications for spatial working memory task acquisition
papers.summary: This study shows that hippocampal input to prefrontal VIP interneurons weakens with activity, reconfiguring inhibitory microcircuits and impairing spatial working memory task learning in mice. The findings implicate this pathway as a key locus of plasticity linked to cognitive deficits.

papers.title: Electroencephalogram Utilization, Epileptiform Findings, and Associated Factors Among Children with Epilepsy in Southwestern Uganda: A 5-Year Retrospective Record Review.
papers.summary: This retrospective record review of 427 children with epilepsy in southwestern Uganda found that only 34.9% had undergone EEG, with epileptiform EEGs in 68.5% of those. Female sex and generalized seizures were independently associated with higher likelihood of epileptiform EEGs, highlighting the need for increased EEG use and training.

papers.title: Personalized in silico modeling of cardiac ion channel variants to predict drug-induced proarrhythmia risk.
papers.summary: This computational study integrates genetic variants in hERG and Nav1.5 channels to simulate amiodarone effects across five human cardiac cell types. The results reveal genotype- and cell-type-specific differences in APD90 and qNet, highlighting midmyocardial vulnerability and the potential of Purkinje cells as silent proarrhythmic substrates, supporting a precision cardiotoxicity screening platform.

papers.title: Clinical and immunological correlates of elevated age-adjusted QAlb in anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 103 patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis, elevated age-adjusted QAlb was associated with increased markers of intrathecal IgG synthesis but not with disease severity or short-term outcomes. The findings suggest QAlb reflects blood-CSF barrier function rather than serving as a standalone prognostic marker.

papers.title: Reliability of Bonini's semiological classification in frontal lobe seizures: A video-EEG based study.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: This study evaluated the reliability of Bonini's semiological classification in frontal lobe seizures using video-EEG recordings from 33 patients, finding excellent intraobserver reliability and substantial interobserver agreement. The classification showed correlations with neuroimaging and surgical outcomes in a subset of patients, supporting its utility as a reproducible framework for presurgical evaluation.

papers.title: Photouncaging of an Opioid Peptide in Vivo Using Blue Light.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: This study introduces TCA-DCCM-DAMGO, a blue light-cleavable caged MOR agonist, demonstrating light-triggered activation in brain slices and in vivo in the mouse VTA, leading to opioid-dependent locomotion. The findings establish blue light photouncaging as feasible for deep brain manipulation and provide a new tool for studying opioid receptors in behaving animals.

papers.title: Steroid-responsive Encephalopathy Associated with Autoimmune Thyroiditis: A Case Fulfilling Definite Graus Criteria.
papers.journal: Journal of community hospital internal medicine perspectives
papers.summary: This case report describes a 70-year-old woman with SREAT presenting with encephalopathy despite thyroid normalization, which responded dramatically to high-dose prednisone, fulfilling definite Graus criteria. It emphasizes distinguishing SREAT from myxedema coma and avoiding overinterpretation of low-titer GAD65 antibodies.

papers.title: Engineered multicolor "Fluorescent Lantern" TEC-Fusion protein with tunable spectra enables multiplexed fluorescent labeling and biological imaging.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.summary: The paper reports the design and characterization of TEC-Fusion, a tricolor fluorescent fusion protein composed of mTagBFP2, EGFP, and mCherry, which enables multiplexed imaging across seven visible spectra including white and magenta. It demonstrates good stability, biocompatibility, and imaging capability in cells, composite materials, and animal models.

papers.title: Othello syndrome as an early manifestation of Alzheimer's disease: an anatomoclinical case study.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 54-year-old patient with Alzheimer's disease whose initial manifestation was Othello syndrome, characterized by delusional jealousy. Postmortem examination confirmed Alzheimer's pathology with senile plaques and neurofibrillary tangles.

papers.title: Education Research: Development of a Workplace-Based Assessment to Enhance EEG Interpretation Skills for Medical Students.
papers.summary: This prospective study developed and evaluated a workplace-based assessment (WBA) for medical students during a 2-week EEG elective, involving 79 WBAs with 20 students. The tool was feasible and educationally valuable, with a significant decrease in high-level assistance needed from week 1 to week 2, indicating its effectiveness in enhancing EEG interpretation skills.

papers.title: Green synthesis of N-aryl-1-(2-bromo-4-methyl phenyl)-1H-tetrazol-5-amines as novel anti-cancer agents targeting tubulin-Combretastatin A4 complex and human non-small cell lung cancer cell lines.
papers.summary: The paper describes the microwave-assisted synthesis of N-aryl-1-(2-bromo-4-methyl phenyl)-1H-tetrazol-5-amines and evaluates their anti-lung cancer activity against A549, EKVX, and NCI-H460 cell lines. Two compounds showed potent anti-proliferative activity, with docking studies indicating binding to the colchicine pocket of tubulin.

papers.title: Machine learning and molecular docking-driven identification of novel umami peptides from pea protein and electroencephalography (EEG) neural mechanisms analysis of their umami-enhancing effects.
papers.summary: This study used machine learning and molecular docking to identify novel umami peptides from pea protein, and validated their umami-enhancing effects using sensory evaluation, electronic tongue, and EEG analysis. The peptides enhanced umami perception, elicited specific neural oscillations in theta, alpha, and beta bands, and showed strong activation in parietal and parieto-occipital regions, with key receptor-binding sites identified.

papers.title: A Biomimetic Nanoplatform Alleviates Depression via GRP75-Targeted Mitochondria-Associated Endoplasmic Reticulum Membranes Disassembly and Nanozyme-Driven ROS Scavenging.
papers.summary: This study developed a macrophage-biomimetic nanoplatform (P/F-Rg1@M) encapsulating ginsenoside Rg1 and an Fe3O4 nanozyme to target microglia and alleviate depression. In chronic social defeat stress mice, the nanomedicine disrupted GRP75-mediated MAM contacts, scavenged ROS, restored hippocampal neuron firing and gamma oscillations, and reduced depressive-like behaviors, with effects abolished in microglia-specific GRP75 knockout mice.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
